# Rule of 100, Open To Goal & The Roadmap

**Source:** *$100M Leads*, Section V "Get Started" (lines ~4175–4528).
This is the "just do it" layer: the **volume rule** that makes any advertising work, the **effort
standard** for elite operators, the **one-page plan** for a day's work, and the **roadmap sequence**
from your first lead to a $100M machine. `hormozi-lead-roadmap` runs this.

---

## 1 — The Volume Lesson (why nothing works without it)

Most people **dramatically underestimate the volume** advertising takes and **stop too soon** (l.4317).
Hormozi's flyer story: he put out **300** flyers and got zero leads; his mentor tested with **5,000**,
then ran **5,000 per day, every day, for a month** — Hormozi had done **1/1500th** of the required
effort (l.4305, l.4319). The refrain he hears constantly (l.4321):
> *"I reached out to 100 people over six weeks and got one customer, it doesn't work."* → "You did
> **1/42** of the work. It was **100 per day**, not 100 over time."

Advertising is an **inputs-and-outputs game**: you input advertising effort, your output is engaged
leads. Never let *effort* be the reason something failed — it can be the offer, copy, image, targeting,
media, or platform, *"but not. my. effort."* (l.4313).

---

## 2 — The Rule of 100 (the baseline)

> **Do 100 primary actions every day, for 100 days in a row** (l.2792–2794).

The one promise in the book: 100 primary actions/day × 100 straight days **will** get you more engaged
leads. Applied to each Core Four activity (l.2796–2826):

| Core Four activity | Daily target | Example primary actions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Warm Reach Outs** | **100 reach outs**/day | email, text, DM, calls | to people who know you |
| **Post Content** | **100 minutes**/day making content | short/long videos or articles, podcasts, infographics | release ≥1/day per platform; post more as you improve |
| **Cold Reach Outs** | **100 reach outs**/day | email, text, DM, cold call, flyers | expect lower response — **use automation** |
| **Paid Ads** | **100 minutes**/day making paid ads | direct-response media ads, direct mail, seminar, podcast spots | run **100 days straight**; use your daily budget; aim for **Client-Financed Acquisition** |

**Keep the units exact:** outreach = **100 actions**; content and paid ads = **100 minutes of
production**.

---

## 3 — Open To Goal (the Rule of 100 "on steroids")

A gym chain let sales managers set their own hours **on one condition: sign up five new members per day,
no matter what** — done by lunch, leave early; takes 18 hours, so be it. They called it **open-to-goal**
(l.4327).

- The Rule of 100 commits you to a number of **actions**. **Open To Goal commits you to a number of
  outcomes** — you work until you hit the result, *no matter what* (l.4329). It might take 50 attempts,
  or 5,000 every day for years.
- The standard: *"Give up the idea of 'doing your best.' Instead, do what is required"* (l.4331) —
  sometimes your best just has to get better.

### How Hormozi makes Open To Goal work — the habit stack (l.4333–4353)

1. **Wake up early (4–5 am)** — which really means **go to bed early**.
2. **Get right to work** — no rituals, no routines; coffee, then work.
3. **No meetings until noon** — uninterrupted, fully focused work time.

The magic isn't the early hour; it's a **long stretch of uninterrupted work right after a long stretch
of uninterrupted sleep** — the most productive hours doing the most productive work. This "habit stack"
(wake early → work immediately → ~8 hours straight) is his highest-ROI habit by a longshot. Set the
daily goal to what you know you can do; only *after* the work block do you fight fires and talk to people.

---

## 4 — The One-Page Advertising Checklist (a day's plan in 5 steps)

Skip the 100-page plan nobody uses; a single page "leaves little room for excuses, distractions, and
delusions" and takes ~5 minutes to fill (l.4359–4385):

1. **Pick the type of engaged lead to get:** Customers, Affiliates, Employees, or Agencies.
2. **Pick Rule of 100 or Open To Goal.** Commit to your daily advertising actions.
3. **Fill out the advertising checklist** for that daily action.
4. **Do that daily action** until you have enough money to pay someone else to do it.
5. **When you do, go back to Step 1** — make **Employees** your new target lead type, repeat Steps 1–4
   until you have the help you need, then scale again.

---

## 5 — The Roadmap: Zero to $100,000,000 (l.4387–4435)

The phases Acquisition.com uses to scale portfolio companies. Note the **primary action** at each level
— this is the order a beginner adds methods.

- **Level 1 — Your friends know about the stuff you sell.** One offer, one avatar, one platform. The
  moment you get engaged leads, you can make money.
  → **Primary action: Warm outreach.**

- **Level 2 — You consistently let everyone you know about your stuff.** You know the exact inputs to
  get a lead and scale them to *consistent* customers by maxing your personal work capacity. *(Hormozi
  used paid ads with a case-study lead magnet, but says he wishes he'd started with posting free content
  — so he recommends that.)*
  → **Primary actions: as much warm outreach + post as much content as you can, consistently.**

- **Level 3 — You get employees to help you advertise.** You've maxed *your* inputs but not the
  platform; more leads means doing more. *(He hired a videographer and a media buyer.)*
  → **Primary action: hire people to advertise profitably on your behalf.**

- **Level 4 — Your product is good enough to get consistent referrals.** Build goodwill and aim for
  **25%+ of customers from referrals**; update the product on customer feedback (he did it every two
  weeks) and run a strong referral program. *Most people mess up here by letting the product slip.*
  → **Primary actions: fix the product until referrals are consistent, then resume scaling with a
  bigger team.**

- **Level 5 — You advertise in more places, more ways, with more people.** Expand to new audiences on
  your best platform → use all placements/media types it supports → once the team gets consistent
  results, expand to **another platform, lead-getter, or Core Four activity.** *(This is the "New" of
  More-Better-New at team scale, and where his affiliate program was born.)*
  → **Primary action: advertise profitably using ≥2 methods on multiple platforms.**

- **Level 6 — You hire killers.** Executives grow departments around a method or platform *without you*
  — experienced leaders, not potential. *(Took him 3 years to learn he needed veteran executives with
  stronger incentives; this is how Acquisition.com crossed $100M then $200M+.)*
  → **Primary action: battle-hardened executives/department heads take over new activities and channels.**

- **Level 7 —** *"I'll come back and edit this chapter once I cross a billion."*

**Timeframe:** for owners who know what to do, the $100M machine takes roughly **five to ten years**
(Hormozi's own first $100M net worth took 10+ years) — *"play games where if you wait, you win"* (l.4461).

### What the $100M machine looks like (l.4437–4459)

Media team scaling tons of free content across platforms · regular offers to a warm audience for
customers/affiliates · a ravenous audience that makes any launch immediately profitable · teams running
and scaling paid ads on multiple platforms · a cold-outreach team · an affiliate manager launching and
integrating affiliates · recruiters and recruiting agencies bringing in lead getters · a product so
good a third of customers refer · and an executive team driving it all **without you**.

## The full beginner sequence (putting it together)

The order that happens naturally across the whole system — the Core Four first, then Lead Getters
(l.2914, l.4167, l.4397–4429):

1. **Warm outreach first** — seed your pool of customers from people who already know you.
2. **Then add a second Core Four by resource:** more time than money → **post content**; more money than
   time → **cold outreach or paid ads**. (Only do **one** to start, then max it out.)
3. **More → Better → New** on that activity (see `more-better-new.md`).
4. **Employees** — hire people to do the advertising once you can afford it.
5. **Referrals** — get the product good enough that customers refer (target 25%+).
6. **Agencies** — buy skills for new methods/platforms and transfer them to your team.
7. **Affiliates** — recruit an army that eventually runs on its own.

*Sub-skill routing:* `more-better-new.md` for scaling a single activity; `lead-getters.md` (## Referrals
/ ## Employees / ## Agencies / ## Affiliates) for each lead getter.

---

## A Decade in a Page (the whole book, distilled — l.4486–4528)

1. Define a lead → you're after **engaged leads**, not just leads.
2. Turn leads into engaged leads with an **offer or lead magnet**.
3. **The Core Four** — the only four ways to let people know about your stuff:
   a. Warm outreach → *ask them if they know anybody.*
   b. Post content → *hook, retain, reward; give until they ask.*
   c. Cold outreach → *lists, personalization, big fast value, volume.*
   d. Paid ads → *targeting, callouts, What-Who-Whens, CTAs, Client-Financed Acquisition.*
4. **Maximize the Core Four: More, Better, New** — "what stops us from doing 10x the volume?"; find the
   constraint, test More until it frees, then repeat.
5. **The Four Lead Getters: Customers, Employees, Agencies, Affiliates.**
6. **Advertising in the real world: the Rule of 100 and Open To Goal** — plus the five-step one-page plan.
7. **The seven levels of advertisers** and the *$100M Leads* machine in action.

**The many-sided die (l.4534–4584):** you can't see how many sides your die has; only that green (a win)
appears rarely at first. Every green roll turns one red side green, so wins compound the more you roll.
The two guarantees: *(1) the more you roll, the better you get; (2) if you quit, you lose.* The final
promise — **"You cannot lose if you do not quit."**

---

## Output contract for `hormozi-lead-roadmap`

Given where the user is now, produce:
1. **Their current Level (1–6)** on the roadmap, with the evidence that places them there.
2. **The next level's primary action** and what to build to reach it.
3. **A filled One-Page Advertising Checklist** — lead type, Rule of 100 *or* Open To Goal, the daily
   action + its checklist, and the trigger to hand it off and re-target Employees.
4. **The Rule-of-100 daily number** for their chosen activity (100 actions or 100 minutes) — never
   softened below 100/day.
5. Any numbers grounded in the product's real economics or marked `<placeholder>` — never fabricated.
